content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods (first 10 days) and overestimates in late periods (last 10 days), suggesting a lagged response to price trends.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 64.84, 71.64) — model reacts too aggressively, peaking too early and then falling too fast.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to revert to historical mean too quickly, missing sustained upward momentum.
- Forecast drift: model shows increasing bias toward higher prices as the horizon extends, especially in the last 10 days.
- Underestimation of volatility in early periods — model flattens out too early, missing upward momentum.
- Overestimation of downward momentum in late periods — model assumes prices will fall when they’re actually stabilizing or rising.
